findings.title: MetricAlertDetectorHandler is now abstract and cannot be instantiated
findings.body: MetricAlertDetectorHandler now subclasses StatefulDetectorHandler with only `pass`. StatefulDetectorHandler leaves several abstract members unimplemented: counter_names, get_dedupe_value, get_group_key_values and build_occurrence_and_event_data. Any call to `detector.detector_handler` for a metric_alert_fire detector will therefore raise TypeError when it tries to instantiate the abstract class. Before this change the handler was a concrete no-op.

findings.title: PriorityLevel(new_status) fails for detector levels with no PriorityLevel equivalent
findings.body: The code converts a DetectorPriorityLevel to PriorityLevel by value. If DetectorPriorityLevel defines any non-OK value that PriorityLevel does not have, this raises ValueError and aborts evaluation for the whole packet. The surrounding state updates have already been enqueued at that point, so the enqueued state is left inconsistent with what was actually processed.

findings.title: Test builds expected occurrences with wrong values, hiding mismatches
findings.body: Several tests build the expected occurrence with value=6 even though the evaluated value is 10, 100 or 8. In TestEvaluateGroupKeyValue the expected occurrence also uses group key 'val1' while the code evaluates 'group_key'. These tests only pass because the mock ignores both the value and, effectively, the fingerprint in a way that coincidentally matches. As a result the assertions do not verify that the correct value and group key are passed to build_occurrence_and_event_data.
